newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-LOPEZ HOMER GIVES BRAVES GAME ONE IN LOS ANGELES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-LOPEZ HOMER GIVES BRAVES GAME ONE IN LOS ANGELES.

text.p: Javy Lopez homered in the 10th inning and John Smoltz held the Dodgers to one run as the World Series champion Atlanta Braves edged Los Angeles 2-1 in the opener of their National League divisional playoff series on Wedensday.
Lopez led off the 10th inning by driving a 3-2 pitch from reliever Antonio Osuna (0-1) into the bleachers in right-centre field to give Atlanta the upper hand in the best-of-five series.
"He hung it a bit and I just tried to drive it," said Lopez, of the home run pitch. "I wasn't sure it was out.
"I waited a long time to play with this team and a long time for something like this," added the longtime backup, now the Braves starting catcher.
Smoltz, who led the majors with 24 wins this season, gave up just four hits in nine innings with two walks and seven strikeouts, raising his career post-season record to 6-1.
Braves closer Mark Wohlers allowed a single to Greg Gagne in the bottom of the 10th, but struck out two for his fifth career post-season save.

Smoltz dueled Dodgers starter Ramon Martinez for most of the game. Martinez left for a pinch-hitter in the bottom of the eighth after allowing one run and three hits with three walks and six strikeouts.
Atlanta, which rode its fifth straight division title into the playoffs, grabbed the lead in the fourth.
Marquis Grissom hit a leadoff single, stole second, moved to third on Mark Lemke's groundout and scored on Fred McGriff's sacrifice fly.
Los Angeles tied the game in the fifth on doubles by Gagne and Todd Hollandsworth, who sliced a shot down the left-field line, bringing home Gagne.
But Smoltz shut the Dodgers down the rest of the way, retiring the last 13 batters he faced.
"I'm disappointed. We worked hard for this and we really wanted to win the first game," said Hollandsworth.
The Braves nearly avoided extra innings but they left a man stranded on third in the eighth when Lemke bounced to second to end the inning.
The Dodgers had only one runner over the final five innings with all their scoring chances coming early.
Los Angeles, the league's wild card team, squandered an opportunity to pick up a run in the third inning when Eric Karros fouled out with runners on first and third.
"We had opportunities, but that's why he has 24 victories. He doesn't let guys score," Dodgers manager Bill Russell said of Smoltz.
Game Two is scheduled for Thursday in Los Angeles.
Said Braves manager Bobby Cox: "We came here for a split but now we want to win both."
